specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: two friendly cartoon clouds of small floating dots hovering in an open space, one cloud tinted soft blue labeled by nothing (the real images) and one cloud tinted warm orange (the generated images), partly overlapping like two soap bubbles drifting together. A cheerful cartoon measuring character stands between them stretching a soft tape measure across the gap between the two cloud centers, smiling as it reads the distance. Tiny cartoon photo-thumbnails of dogs drift inside both clouds, sitting close together, while a single thumbnail of TV static floats far off to the side, alone and ignored. Friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive, minimal clutter, generous margins, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable. One clear visual metaphor: measuring quality as the distance between two distributions of features.
specs.alt: Two overlapping clouds of floating dots, one soft blue for real images and one warm orange for generated images, with a cartoon character stretching a tape measure across the gap between their centers while dog-photo thumbnails cluster inside both clouds and a lone TV-static thumbnail drifts far away, picturing how FID and KID score a generator by the distance between whole feature distributions rather than per-image error.
specs.caption: With no reference image to compare against, you stop scoring single pictures and start measuring how far one cloud of features sits from another.

specs.anchorText: synthetic data is salt, not bread; it seasons a real meal and ruins one made entirely of itself
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background, gently split into two scenes. Left scene: a cheerful cartoon chef robot at a stove seasoning a hearty plate of real food (the real dataset) with a small shaker of orange salt (the synthetic data), the dish looking balanced and appetizing. Right scene: a worried cartoon photocopier-robot copying a face, then copying the copy, then copying that copy, in a little descending row of three faces that grow blander, paler, and more identical each time, the rare quirky details fading from the corners, illustrating model collapse. A faint divider separates the two scenes. Friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, generous margins, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear visual metaphor: synthetic data as seasoning that helps in moderation but, fed to itself recursively, collapses into a bland copy.
specs.alt: A two-scene cartoon: on the left a chef robot seasons a real meal with a shaker of orange synthetic salt, on the right a photocopier robot copies a face, then the copy, then the copy of the copy, each one blander and more identical as the rare details fade, illustrating that synthetic data helps as a supplement to real data but recursively training on its own output causes model collapse.
specs.caption: Synthetic data is salt, not bread: it seasons a real dataset, but a model fed only its own output photocopies itself into a bland, collapsed caricature.

specs.anchorText: Any artifact a detector keys on becomes a loss term the next generator is trained to remove.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a proud cartoon detective-detector character holds up a freshly published poster pinned to a board, showing a magnified telltale fingerprint pattern it has learned to catch (drawn as a simple wavy spectral squiggle). Right beside it, a sly but not menacing cartoon generator robot peeks over its shoulder, copies that exact squiggle onto its own checklist, and erases it from its next output with a small eraser, so the new image it holds is now smooth and clean. A small calendar leaf flutters between them suggesting time passing, and the detective looks deflated. Friendly and approachable like a comic strip or XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, generous margins, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor, never mean-spirited. One clear visual metaphor: publishing a detector hands the answer key to an adversary who always moves last.
specs.alt: A cartoon detector character proudly pins up a poster of the telltale spectral fingerprint it learned to catch, while a sly generator robot peeks over its shoulder, copies that exact pattern onto a checklist, and erases it from its next clean output as a calendar leaf flutters past, illustrating why deepfake detection loses the arms race when every published artifact becomes a loss term the next generator removes.
specs.caption: Publishing a deepfake detector is handing over the answer key: every artifact you announce becomes the very thing the next generator is trained to erase.

specs.anchorText: A post-hoc watermark is a sticker on the bumper; an in-generation watermark is the VIN stamped into the chassis.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background. Two friendly cartoon cars side by side. The first car has a flimsy paper sticker peeling off its bumper that a small hand is effortlessly lifting away (the post-hoc watermark). The second car has its identifying mark deeply stamped into the metal of its chassis, glowing faintly from within the body itself, impossible to peel (the in-generation watermark woven into the weave). Above and connecting them, a tidy horizontal chain of three small signed-document cards linked by little padlocks runs left to right (capture, edit, publish), ending at a friendly inspector character holding a checkmark stamp, representing the cryptographically signed C2PA manifest chain. Friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive, minimal clutter, generous margins, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable. One clear visual metaphor: provenance as a stamped-in identity plus a signed, tamper-evident chain of custody.
specs.alt: Two cartoon cars compare a peeling paper bumper sticker being lifted away against an identifying mark stamped deep into the chassis and glowing from within, while above them a chain of three padlock-linked signed-document cards for capture, edit, and publish leads to an inspector with a checkmark stamp, contrasting a removable post-hoc watermark with an in-generation watermark and a tamper-evident C2PA provenance manifest.
specs.caption: A post-hoc watermark peels off like a bumper sticker; an in-generation watermark is stamped into the chassis, and a signed manifest adds a tamper-evident chain of custody on top.

specs.anchorText: data, weights, outputs: three locks, three keys, and only one of them is still being cut
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon engineer character stands before a tall door bearing three stacked locks, one above the other. The bottom lock (training data) is the largest and busiest, surrounded by little floating photo thumbnails and a tiny gavel hovering nearby to suggest it is the most litigated. The middle lock (model weights) is a clean padlock that the engineer is calmly opening with a key labelled by a simple document icon. The top lock (generated outputs) is still being shaped on a tiny key-cutting wheel by a small puzzled locksmith, its key half-finished, to show it is unresolved. The engineer holds two finished keys and looks confidently at the unfinished third. Friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, generous margins, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear visual metaphor: the three legal layers as three locks, two openable today and one still being cut.
specs.alt: A cartoon engineer faces a door with three stacked locks: a large bottom lock for training data ringed by photo thumbnails and a tiny gavel marking it the most litigated, a middle lock for model weights being opened with a document-shaped key, and a top lock for generated outputs whose key is still half-finished on a locksmith's cutting wheel, picturing the three-layer legal stack where two layers are resolvable today and output ownership remains unsettled.
specs.caption: Data, weights, and outputs are three separate locks: you can cut two of the keys today by reading the documents, and the third is still being shaped in the courts.
